description: Winning Points review, checked 20 Nov 2026: no products on sale, a 49% six season rival tally, tracker records 2015 to 2026 and what readers say.
dek: A New York football newsletter that dates itself to 1970. On 20 Nov 2026 its signup page still listed no products, its home page pointed readers to a phone line about 2025 football, and the forum trackers we read had no Winning Points plays to grade in 2025 or 2026. Every multi season tally we found lands near break even before the vig.

short_answer: Winning Points is a real, long running football newsletter. A named New York company publishes it, the site gives a street address, two phone numbers and written legal terms, and its weekly issues were shared and tracked on betting forums from at least 2015 to 2024. In that sense it is a legitimate publication, not a phantom tout.

What it sells today is unclear. On 20 Nov 2026 the online signup page listed no products, the home page asked readers to call a Long Island number for information on 2025 football, the site's security certificate had expired and its home page printed database error messages. Forum trackers that grade many newsletters every week, on SBR and TheRX, listed Winning Points at 0 wins and 0 losses for the whole 2025 season and for 2026 through 10 Nov, which suggests no issues reached the forums in either season.

On results, every outside number we found points to roughly break even before the vig, which means a small loss at normal odds. A rival newsletter's six season table put Winning Points best bets at 49.13%. Forum tallies we could open came to 29 and 31 for one season, 20 and 21 with a push at mid November 2019, and 29 and 33 for 2022. The one strong stretch we found was a partial 2015 tally of 33 and 18 with a push. Readers mostly describe it as useful reading, not a service to follow blindly.
pricing_intro: We found no price on 20 Nov 2026. The membership signup page showed no products, and the FAQ describes plan types (monthly, six months, full year and single issue or one day access) without prices. The home page lists a toll free number and a 1-900 line for phone plays with no rates, and a separate page says to call 1-516-628-0426, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 9 am to 5 pm ET, "for info on 2025 NFL & Coll Football." The basketball page says delivery can be by mail, email, web site or newsstand.

guarantee: We found no guarantee, refund promise or free extension anywhere on the pages we opened on 20 Nov 2026. The FAQ only explains how to cancel an automatic monthly renewal: "You can cancel your subscription at least 2 business days prior to the due renewal date by Logging in to your membership profile page and clicking the "Cancel". link near the bottom of the page."

The FAQ adds: "No cancellation needed for the Full Year, 6 Months and Single Issue / 1 Day Access accounts, since they are not automatically renewed after expiration unless you specifically requested so." The legal terms page is a privacy policy last dated 2004 and says nothing about refunds.

Losses on bets are never covered by any newsletter, and they are usually far larger than the subscription price. Because no product was for sale online when we checked, anyone buying by phone should ask for the refund terms in writing first.

claims_note: How we checked: the only Winning Points record the publisher shows is the 2015 sample issue, so we read all 14 pages of it and compared its claims with the site's own dates. We then recomputed every outside tally we cite from the raw win and loss counts.

The age claims mostly hang together. Volume 46 in the fall of 2015 points to a first volume around 1970, which matches the About page. The newsstand sentence does not: 32 years after 1970 is 2002, and the About page has clearly not been edited since then.

The headline numbers are chosen runs. The sample issue leads with an 11 play phone record from the first weeks of one season, and the WP Ultra page quotes a 60% revenge record without a single dated play behind it. Neither tells you how the paid plays did over a full season.

The outside numbers are dull by comparison. Recomputed from the Powers' Picks table: 236 / (236 + 234) = 50.21% in college, 190 / (190 + 207) = 47.86% in the NFL and 426 / (426 + 441) = 49.13% combined. At standard odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: no full, time stamped log of every Winning Points pick from the publisher. The closest things are a rival's results table and several seasons of forum tracking, each of which graded the newsletter's star rated plays at the line printed in the issue.

A spring 2021 issue of Powers' Picks, a rival newsletter, printed a table of football newsletter results for the 2015 to 2020 regular seasons. It listed Winning Points Best Bets and Preferred plays at 236 and 234 with 10 pushes in college (50.21%), 190 and 207 with 10 pushes in the NFL (47.86%), and 426 and 441 with 20 pushes combined (49.13%). The rival ranked itself first in the same table, so it has an interest, but the method was the same for every newsletter listed.

A member of TheRX who has tracked newsletters there for over a decade posted these Winning Points season tallies: a partial 2015 count covering only 13 issues of 33 and 18 with a push (NCAA 4 star 8 and 4 with a push, 3 star 9 and 2, NFL 4 star 8 and 6, 3 star 8 and 6, as of 22 Dec 2015); a full prior season, posted in July 2017, of 29 and 31 (NCAA 4 star 5 and 8, 3 star 8 and 5, NFL 4 star 7 and 10, 3 star 9 and 8); and 20 and 21 with a push for 2019 through 12 Nov (NCAA 4 star 4 and 7, 3 star 7 and 4, NFL 4 star 4 and 6, 3 star 5 and 4 with a push).

For 2022 another tracker on TheRX posted college 4 star 10 and 4, college 3 star 8 and 6, NFL 4 star 5 and 13 and NFL 3 star 6 and 10 with 2 pushes, which adds up to 29 and 33. The same weekly tracker that grades Gold Sheet, Power Sweep, Playbook and others then showed every Winning Points line at 0 and 0 in its final 2025 numbers (through 8 Feb 2026) and again on 10 Nov 2026. Adding the full seasons and partial counts we found, other than the strong partial 2015 count, gives 78 and 85 with 3 pushes, or 47.9%.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Winning Points pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Winning Points performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the outside tallies we found put Winning Points near 48% to 50% on its top plays. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: We found no buyer reviews of Winning Points on review sites. What exists is forum talk from readers who follow football newsletters, plus forum trackers that grade its plays. Below is everything we found, oldest patterns first in the summary, and how much weight each item can carry.

customers.text: We read about 17 relevant forum posts on TheRX, SBR and Covers from 2015 to 2026, plus one rival newsletter's results table. Nobody described a billing problem, a refund fight or pushy sales calls, which are the common complaints about phone touts. Instead the talk is about whether the picks win. The positive side: in 2015 the star rated football plays were well ahead over 13 issues, one member in 2017 called it among the best in the business and shared it every week, and in 2023 a member said it led the way the season before. The negative side: full season tallies came to 29 and 31, about 20 and 21 at mid season 2019, and 29 and 33 in 2022; members told others to fade it after a bad weekend in 2020 and said in 2023 and 2024 that newsletters like it are for reading, not betting. Since 2025 the trackers show no Winning Points plays at all. Because issues were usually posted free on forums, most of these readers were not paying customers.

A TheRX member who tracks newsletters posted Winning Points football Best Bets at 33 wins, 18 losses and a push, noting the count covered only 13 of that season's issues. College 3 star plays were 9 and 2. The same week a reposted tally put its basketball best bets at 13 and 9 in college and 25 and 17 in the NBA, while a bowl tracker had Winning Points at 1 and 4.

A TheRX member said they had shared Winning Points with the forum early every Tuesday the season before and would do it again, calling it and a totals newsletter among the best in the business. The thread's tracker thanked them and posted that season's Winning Points record at 29 wins and 31 losses across its four star levels.

The TheRX tracker's 2019 update showed Winning Points college 3 star plays at 7 and 4 but college 4 star plays at 4 and 7, for 20 wins, 21 losses and a push overall. Two weeks earlier the newsletter had gone 0 and 4 in a single weekend.

After a losing weekend, one TheRX member told others to add Winning Points to their fade list. Another member pointed out that the link posted for that week was the previous week's issue, and the poster fixed it.

Reposting the final 2025 numbers before the new season, the TheRX tracker listed every Winning Points category at 0 wins and 0 losses for the year, while grading hundreds of plays from other newsletters. The same blank line had appeared in November 2025.
On TheRX, a member answering a claim that only two newsletters had winning records said Winning Points led the way the season before and had started the new season 3 and 1.

A tracker in the same thread posted the 2022 numbers: college plays were winning (10 and 4 on 4 star, 8 and 6 on 3 star) while NFL plays lost (5 and 13 on 4 star, 6 and 10 on 3 star). The tracker listed the NFL 4 star among the worst records of that season.

On Covers, a bettor said they use Pointwise, Winning Points and Northcoast. Another member replied that these are all losing publications, but that they can still be useful for stats and for reading the general consensus.
On SBR, when a member suggested several newsletters including Winning Points, another said they are only for reading and told people to think twice before betting the picks.

In the same SBR thread a longtime member said Pointwise and Winning Points have been around for decades but that "the print is too small for me." Another said the newsletters were posted free on the forum every week.

A weekly SBR tracker that grades the best bets of many newsletters showed every Winning Points category at 0 wins and 0 losses for the 2026 season, while it graded dozens of plays for other newsletters. It does not say why.
A Better Business Bureau search for Starpoint Publishing in New York returned no results. Our searches found no buyer review of a paid subscription on any forum we opened.

conflicts: The only multi season record we found was compiled and printed by Powers' Picks, a competing newsletter that ranked itself first. Its numbers for Winning Points may be accurate, but a rival is not a neutral auditor.

Full Winning Points issues were posted free on forums such as TheRX, SBR and BookmakersReview by users for years. That is not a conflict for the publisher, but it means many forum opinions come from readers, not paying subscribers, and the forum trackers can only grade the issues someone chose to post.
Winning Points is not paid by Watchdog and does not advertise with us. We have no link to any sportsbook named on its pages.
strengths: A named company with a New York address, a toll free number, written legal terms and a clear FAQ on cancelling auto renewal.
Long history as a printed newsletter, with full weekly write ups and projected scores on every board game rather than only a few picks.
No reports we found of billing disputes, refund fights or high pressure sales in more than ten years of forum talk.
Its plays were tracked publicly by forum members for several seasons, so a reader can see how the star rated picks did instead of relying on the publisher's runs.
The free 2015 sample issue lets a reader judge the format and depth before paying.
concerns: No products available for purchase on the site on 20 Nov 2026, and no prices shown anywhere.
Outside tallies put the top plays near 48% to 50% across many seasons, below the 52.4% needed at -110.
The site shows signs of neglect: an expired security certificate, database errors on the home page, a 2015 sample issue, a 2004 copyright on the legal terms and a call line for 2025 football.
Seller claims such as a 60% revenge record and a 10 and 1 phone run come with no log or list of plays.
Forum trackers found nothing to grade for 2025 or 2026, so there is no recent independent record at all.
checklist: Call the listed number and ask whether the newsletter is still published this season before you pay anything.
Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the date of the issue. A sample from 2015 is not a record.
Confirm what you are buying, what it costs and the refund terms in writing, since the site lists no prices or refund policy.
If you take a monthly plan, note the renewal date and cancel at least two business days before it.
Count units, not wins. A 50% record at -110 loses money.
Use a newsletter as research, and record any pick you bet with the line you actually got.
faq: It is a real, long running newsletter published by a named New York company with an address and phone numbers. We found no court or regulator action and no billing complaints. Whether its picks win is another matter: the outside tallies we found put its best bets near 48% to 50% over many seasons.
How much does Winning Points cost?
We could not find a price. On 20 Nov 2026 the signup page said no products were available, and the phone lines list no rates. The FAQ mentions monthly, six month, full year and single issue plans.
Does Winning Points have a verified record?

Not from the publisher. A rival newsletter's table for the 2015 to 2020 regular seasons put its Best Bets and Preferred plays at 426 and 441 with 20 pushes, and forum trackers counted 29 and 31 for one full season, 20 and 21 at mid season 2019 and 29 and 33 for 2022.

We could not confirm it. Issues were shared on forums through 2024, but forum trackers graded no Winning Points plays in 2025 or 2026, the signup page sold nothing on 20 Nov 2026 and the home page still pointed to a phone line about 2025 football.
Does Winning Points offer a guarantee or refunds?
We found none. The FAQ only explains how to cancel an automatic monthly renewal two business days before it renews. Ask for refund terms in writing before buying by phone.

As reading material it has depth: write ups and projected scores for every board game. As a betting service, nothing we found shows its plays beating the roughly 52.4% needed at -110, and the most recent seasons have no record at all.
